To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the administration of BMSCs in patients with STEMI treated with PCI is associated with a significant reduction in the number of MVD, a significant increase of the percentage of CD34+ cells in peripheral blood, and a significant reduction in circulating levels of Fractalkine.

the expression of the fractalkine receptor, CX3CR1, was up-regulated on CD34+ cells after treatment with the CX3CL1 ligand, fractalkine, and that these cells were able to differentiate into cells with characteristics of the endothelial lineage.

(1) the use of a 1.5% NaCl solution as a vehicle for intracoronary delivery of autologous CD133+ cells is safe, and (2) the use of this solution as a vehicle is associated with a significant reduction in adverse events at 6 months after the procedure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method for the determination of the mechanical characteristics of soft tissues.
the effects of autologous BMDSC on the inflammatory response and the levels of the CX3CL1/CX3CR1 axis in patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI.
the development and characterization of a novel class of compounds that are capable of inhibiting the interaction of the chemokine fractalkine with its cognate receptor CX3CR1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence for the use of bone marrow stem cell therapy in the treatment of myocardial infarct and heart failure is still insufficient.
the use of autologous stem cell therapy in patients with acute MI is safe and may be effective, but that the data are still too preliminary to allow a definitive conclusion.
the use of autologous BMSCs for the treatment of patients with STEMI is not supported by the available evidence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results are not conclusive and the results are not consistent with each other.
the levels of fractalkine (CX3CL1) are elevated early after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)-treated ST-elevation myocardinal infarction (STEMI).

we have demonstrated that fractalkine is elevated in the early period after acute myocardial infarctions (MI) and that this elevation does not change with autologous bone-marrow derived stem cell (BMDSC) injection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of autologous stem cells in patients with acute myocardial infarctions does not improve the outcome of the patient.
